references.text: Jesus refers to the Passover bread as a symbol of the liberation of Israel's children, which foreshadows his own body broken for humanity's salvation.
The prophecy about the Messiah who would be wounded for our transgressions and crushed for our sins, and by whose wounds we have received healing, points forward to Jesus' sacrifice.
Matthew's account of the Last Supper, where Jesus breaks the bread and gives it to the disciples, parallels Mark's version.
Luke's description of the Last Supper, where Jesus breaks the bread as a symbol of his body given for us.
Jesus speaks of himself as the bread of life that came down from heaven, and that whoever eats this bread will live forever, which foreshadows the Lord's Supper.
Paul repeats the words from the Last Supper, emphasizing the significance of Jesus' body and blood as a new covenant.
